Quick Exercise
p ∧ (p ∨ q)
Step 1 Look at the outer operation
● The outer operation is AND
p ∧ (something)
For the whole expression to be True, p must already be True.
● If p is False, then:
False ∧ anything = False
So right away, if p is False, the entire expression is False.
Step 2 What happens if p is True?
Now suppose:
p = True
The expression becomes:
True ∧ True ∨ q)
But:
True ∨ q = True
regardless of what q is.
So we get:
True ∧ True = True
Therefore, whenever p is True, the
whole expression is True.
Step 3 Compare the results
We have discovered:
If p is False → expression is False
If p is True → expression is True
So the entire expression always has the exact same value as p.
Truth Table
p q p ∨ q p ∧ (p ∨ q)

Feedback Loop
A feedback loop occurs when:
● The output eventually feeds back into an earlier input
These circuits behave differently from ordinary combinational circuits
Important idea:
● Feedback allows a circuit to maintain information
● This is important for computer memory
